biography.plain_text: Robert Maxwell was a Czechoslovak-born British publisher who built his fortune through Oxford-based Pergamon Press before acquiring major newspaper and printing businesses. His holdings included Mirror Group Newspapers and Maxwell Communication Corporation. He also served as Labour MP for Buckingham and expanded into American publishing through the acquisition of Macmillan.

long_biography.plain_text:
The publisher Robert Maxwell saw an international market for scientific research at a time when many journals served national scholarly communities. Having escaped continental Europe during the war, he served in the British Army and won the Military Cross. His postwar work in Germany introduced him to publishers whose scientific books and periodicals he could distribute abroad.

At Pergamon, he commissioned journals for emerging specialisms, translated Soviet research and published international conference proceedings. The business connected researchers across national boundaries and drew on the expansion of publicly funded science. His wider companies eventually accumulated debts they could not sustain. After his death in 1991, their collapse exposed his use of employees' pension assets to support the businesses, leaving pensioners facing losses.
